subject: science1
loDesc: Differentiates distance vs displacement, speed vs velocity, uniform vs non-uniform motion, derives equations of motion using graphical methods, and verifies Newton's three laws of motion.
hookDemo: Place a coin on a stiff card resting on a glass tumbler. Flick the card horizontally with a sudden snap.
hookAsk: Why does the card fly off while the coin falls straight into the glass tumbler?
streamDo: Observe an athlete running once around a 400 m circular track and returning to the starting point.
streamTask: Calculate the total distance covered versus net displacement on your worksheet.
mountainTask: Calculate the force (F = m*a) required to accelerate a 1200 kg car from rest to 20 m/s in 10 seconds.
skyTask: Derive Newton's second equation of motion s = ut + (1/2)at^2 using a velocity-time graph.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Believing a continuous external force is required to keep an object moving at a constant speed.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'If an ice hockey puck slides on frictionless ice, does it keep moving or stop when you stop pushing it?' Explain Newton's First Law.

crossCurricularLinks: Math 2: Coordinate Geometry (Plotting motion vectors and analyzing velocity-time graph slopes)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Calculates motion parameters and derives kinematical equations using velocity-time graphs.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Conduct toy car ramp experiments to collect velocity-time data for graphing.

subject: science1
loDesc: Calculates work done (W = F*s*cos theta), kinetic energy (1/2 mv^2), potential energy (mgh), verifies Law of Conservation of Energy, and calculates electrical power.
hookDemo: Release a simple pendulum bob from a stretched height h and let it swing past its lowest equilibrium point.
hookAsk: How does stored potential energy convert into kinetic energy as the bob swings down?
streamDo: Observe scenarios (Pushing a stalled car forward, Applying brakes to stop a moving vehicle, Carrying a heavy bag standing still).
streamTask: Classify work done in each scenario as Positive, Negative, or Zero Work.
mountainTask: Calculate potential energy stored in a 5 kg object raised to a height of 10 m (g = 9.8 m/s^2).
skyTask: Prove mathematically that the total mechanical energy (KE + PE) of a freely falling body remains constant at any point along its path.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Thinking that carrying a heavy suitcase while standing still performs mechanical work.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'If displacement s = 0 in W = F × s, how much work was performed in physics terms?' Distinguish muscular fatigue from mechanical work.

crossCurricularLinks: Environmental Science & Engineering: Hydroelectric Power (Mapping gravitational potential energy conversion in dam turbines)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Calculates kinetic and potential energy and verifies energy conservation laws.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use pendulum bob release heights to measure speed changes experimentally.

subject: science1
loDesc: Verifies Ohm's Law (V = IR), calculates equivalent resistance in series and parallel connections, understands electric power, and safety devices (fuses and MCBs).
hookDemo: Connect two identical 1.5V bulbs first in Series, then in Parallel across a 3V battery cell.
hookAsk: Why do the bulbs glow much brighter in Parallel connection than in Series connection?
streamDo: Observe circuit diagrams showing resistors connected end-to-end vs connected across common nodes.
streamTask: Identify Series vs Parallel resistor arrangements and state their current-voltage distribution rules.
mountainTask: A electric heater draws 5 A current when connected to a 220 V supply. Calculate its resistance using R = V/I.
skyTask: Derive the formula 1/R_p = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2 + 1/R_3 for three resistors connected in parallel.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Assuming electric current is consumed or 'used up' as it flows through resistors in a circuit.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Does the ammeter reading before a resistor equal the ammeter reading after the resistor?' Emphasize charge conservation.

crossCurricularLinks: Electrical Safety & Domestic Wiring: Household Circuits (Explaining why domestic appliances are connected in parallel with MCB safety fuses)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Verifies Ohm's law, calculates equivalent circuit resistances, and understands electrical safety.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Provide ammeters and voltmeters for students to plot V-I graphs in class.

subject: science1
loDesc: Understands Laws of Chemical Combination, Dalton's atomic theory, atomic mass, molecular mass, mole concept, and valencies of polyatomic radicals.
hookDemo: Display a chemical balance showing 18g of water (H2O) alongside 44g of carbon dioxide (CO2).
hookAsk: Why does 18g of water contain the EXACT same number of molecules (6.022 x 10^23) as 44g of carbon dioxide?
streamDo: Observe chemical formulas: H2O, CO2, NaCl, H2SO4.
streamTask: Calculate molecular masses using atomic masses (H=1, O=16, C=12, Na=23, Cl=35.5, S=32).
mountainTask: Calculate the number of moles present in 36 grams of pure water (H2O) using formula Moles = Mass / Molar Mass.
skyTitle: Law of Conservation of Mass Verification
skyTask: Design an experiment using Calcium Chloride and Sodium Sulfate solutions in a conical flask to prove mass conservation during a chemical change.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing one mole of a substance (count of particles) with its mass in grams.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Does a dozen eggs weigh the same as a dozen elephants? They both equal 12 units.' Relate a mole to Avogadro's count.

crossCurricularLinks: Math 1: Ratio and Proportion (Applying stoichiometric mole ratios to chemical reaction mass calculations)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Understands the mole concept, molecular masses, and verifies laws of chemical combination.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use molecular model kits to demonstrate atomic combination ratios.

subject: science1
loDesc: Classifies acids and bases based on Arrhenius theory, measures pH using universal indicator scale, investigates strength of acids/bases, and understands salts and electrolysis.
hookDemo: Dip Universal Indicator paper into lemon juice, milk, pure water, soap solution, and dil. NaOH.
hookAsk: How does the pH color spectrum (1 to 14) indicate whether a substance is a strong acid, weak acid, or base?
streamDo: Observe chemical dissociation equations in water (HCl -> H+ + Cl-, NaOH -> Na+ + OH-).
streamTask: Classify substances as Acids (H+ donors) or Bases (OH- donors) according to Arrhenius theory.
mountainTask: Arrange 4 liquids with pH values 2, 7, 9, 13 in order of increasing H+ ion concentration and classify their acidity/basicity.
skyTask: Draw an electrolysis apparatus for acidified water and explain why the volume of hydrogen gas collected at the cathode is double the oxygen gas at the anode.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Assuming that a higher pH number signifies a stronger acid.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Where is pure water on the pH scale? Which end represents maximum H+ concentration?' Clarify that pH < 7 is acidic (lower pH = stronger acid).

crossCurricularLinks: Environmental Science & Soil Chemistry: Soil Health (Testing pH of agricultural soils to optimize fertilizer selection)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Measures pH values, applies Arrhenius acid-base theory, and investigates electrolysis.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Conduct pH testing on local soil and water samples using universal indicator strips.

subject: science1
loDesc: Investigates spherical mirrors (Concave and Convex), constructs ray diagrams, applies Mirror Formula (1/f = 1/v + 1/u) and Magnification, and analyzes mirror applications.
hookDemo: Display a polished stainless steel spoon. Observe your reflection in the inner curved surface vs the outer curved surface.
hookAsk: Why does the inner surface flip your image upside down while the outer surface keeps it upright and smaller?
streamDo: Observe concave mirror ray diagrams showing Pole (P), Focus (F), Center of Curvature (C), and Principal Axis.
streamTask: Identify and label the key optical points on a given spherical mirror diagram.
mountainTask: An object is placed 15 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Find image position (v) using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u.
skyTask: Construct a precise ray diagram for an object placed between Focus (F) and Center of Curvature (C) of a concave mirror, stating image characteristics.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Ignoring Cartesian sign conventions when substituting object distance u into the mirror formula.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Is the object placed in front of the mirror on the negative X-axis?' Remind that object distance u is always negative.

crossCurricularLinks: Automotive & Solar Engineering: Optical Design (Applying convex mirrors to vehicle rear-view mirrors and concave mirrors to solar furnaces)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Constructs ray diagrams for spherical mirrors and solves optics problems using mirror formulas.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use optical bench setups with concave mirrors and candles for image distance mapping.

subject: science1
loDesc: Explains sound wave propagation (compression and rarefaction), speed of sound in media, reflection of sound, Echo, Reverberation, SONAR, and human ear structure.
hookDemo: Clap two wooden boards together in an empty large hall versus a fully furnished carpeted room.
hookAsk: Why does the clap echo multiple times in the empty hall while sounding dull and immediate in the carpeted room?
streamDo: Observe speed of sound in air at 22°C (344 m/s).
streamTask: Calculate the minimum distance required between a sound source and reflecting surface to hear a distinct echo (time delay >= 0.1 s).
mountainTask: Differentiate Echo (single distinct reflected sound) from Reverberation (persistence of sound due to multiple reflections) and list 2 acoustic absorbers.
skyTask: A SONAR signal sent from a ship returns from the ocean floor after 3 seconds. Calculate sea depth if speed of sound in seawater is 1530 m/s.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Forgetting to divide the total round-trip time by 2 when calculating ocean depth using SONAR echo return signals.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Did the ultrasonic wave travel down AND back up?' Divide time by 2 for one-way distance.

crossCurricularLinks: Marine Navigation & Architecture: Acoustics (Calculating ocean depths with SONAR and designing soundproof auditorium walls)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Calculates speed of sound, echo distances, reverberation control, and SONAR applications.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use slinky spring coils to demonstrate longitudinal compression wave movement.

subject: science1
loDesc: Identifies allotropes of carbon (crystalline: diamond, graphite, fullerene; non-crystalline: coal, charcoal), understands covalent bonding in carbon, and uses of hydrocarbons.
hookDemo: Display a diamond model structure (tetrahedral 3D) alongside a graphite model structure (hexagonal layers).
hookAsk: Why is diamond the hardest natural substance known while graphite is soft and slippery enough to use as a lubricant?
streamDo: Observe carbon forms: Diamond, Graphite, Buckyball Fullerene, Peat Coal, Anthracite.
streamTask: Classify carbon forms into Crystalline Allotropes vs Non-crystalline / Amorphous forms.
mountainTask: Explain why graphite conducts electricity despite being a non-metal, referring to free delocalized electrons in its layer structure.
skyTask: Draw the electron-dot structure and covalent line structure for Methane (CH4) and state 3 physical properties of biogas.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Assuming diamond and graphite are different chemical elements because their physical properties are completely opposite.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'If both burn in pure oxygen to produce identical CO2 gas, are they made of different atoms or different arrangements of carbon?'

crossCurricularLinks: Materials Science & Energy: Renewable Fuel (Evaluating methane biogas generation and carbon nanomaterial structures)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Analyzes carbon allotropes, covalent bonding structures, and hydrocarbon applications.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use pencil lead (graphite) in a simple circuit to test electrical conductivity.

subject: science1
loDesc: Classifies important salts (NaCl, NaHCO3, Na2CO3, Bleaching Powder), radioactive isotopes, food colors, dyes, and artificial sweeteners in daily life.
hookDemo: Add a small amount of Baking Soda (NaHCO3) to dilute Hydrochloric Acid in a test tube.
hookAsk: What gas causes the rapid effervescence, and why is baking soda used in fire extinguishers and cake baking?
streamDo: Observe household substances: Baking Soda, Washing Soda, Bleaching Powder, Plaster of Paris.
streamTask: Match household names with their correct chemical formulas (NaHCO3, Na2CO3.10H2O, CaOCl2, CaSO4.1/2H2O).
mountainTask: Explain how washing soda cleans greasy clothes in hard water and state its water of crystallization.
skyTitle: Radioactive Isotope Applications in Medicine & Industry
skyTask: Explain industrial and medical applications of radioactive isotopes: Cobalt-60 (Cancer therapy), Iodine-131 (Goiter), and Carbon-14 (Dating).

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing Baking Soda (NaHCO3) with Washing Soda (Na2CO3·10H2O).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Which soda releases CO2 gas during baking to make bread rise?' Highlight sodium bicarbonate vs sodium carbonate.

crossCurricularLinks: Medicine & Industrial Chemistry: Nuclear Medicine (Utilizing radioactive tracer isotopes for medical diagnostics and cancer therapy)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Understands chemical preparation and uses of salts, polymers, and radioactive isotopes.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Perform effervescence tests on household baking soda using vinegar.

subject: science1
loDesc: Understands electromagnetic spectrum, visible light telescopes (Refracting and Reflecting: Newtonian, Cassegrain), radio telescopes, and space-based observatories.
hookDemo: Display schematic diagrams of a Refracting Telescope (lenses) vs a Newtonian Reflecting Telescope (concave mirror).
hookAsk: Why do giant modern research observatories use large concave mirrors instead of heavy glass lenses?
streamDo: Observe telescope designs: Refracting (Galilean), Reflecting (Newtonian), Reflecting (Cassegrain), Radio Telescope.
streamTask: Classify telescopes based on whether they use Objective Lenses, Concave Mirrors, or Parabolic Dish Antennas.
mountainTask: Explain why ground-based optical telescopes face atmospheric disturbance and state two advantages of space telescopes like Hubble and James Webb.
skyTitle: ISRO Astrosat & Indian Space Observatories Analysis
skyTask: Write a short technical note on India's multi-wavelength space observatory ASTROSAT and its role in observing celestial sources.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Believing telescopes magnify objects purely by using stronger lenses rather than gathering light with larger objective apertures.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Why do astronomical telescopes need giant primary mirrors or lenses?' Stress light-gathering power over magnification.

crossCurricularLinks: Aerospace Technology: Space Exploration (Analyzing ISRO's ASTROSAT mission and satellite observatory orbits)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Understands optical and radio telescope designs and space-based astronomical observatories.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use convex lens pairs to assemble a simple refracting telescope prototype in class.
